summary: Code map for the three v1.1 changes, built from a full read of octreg/{common,features,search,refine,vascular,evaluate,nonrigid}.py and scripts/{prep_subject,register,viz_result,fig_*,summarize,test_texture_mask}.py plus the run shell scripts. Key findings: (1) the OCT masks are produced in ONE place (prep_subject.py:134 via common.oct_tissue_mask -> histogram_tissue_threshold), and everything downstream (octv_mask 142-144, vessel top-1% 162-163, EDT 168-174, register overlap gate 110-113, OCT Otsu split 97, Refiner weights, density target mask, oct_class, evaluation, all QC/fig scripts) reads oct150_mask.npy / octv_mask.npy, so a mask decision made in prep propagates automatically; the auto fallback can be decided in prep because prep.json already carries mri.tissue_fraction/shape/voxel_mm (loaded at line 35 even with --skip-mri). (2) The destripe slot is prep_subject.py between line 126 (octn, slab = oct_slab_normalize(..., out_dtype=float16); del raw) and 129-130 (pool_mean_np); octn is a 9.4 GB float16 (1457,2013,1595) array with tissue median forced to 16384 and cap 60000 (cap is a local in common.py:204, not returned); cgroup limit 62 GiB / 16 CPUs -> chunked in-place processing only. (3) The fine stage slots in register.py after line 179 / around the vascular block 181-217; Refiner (refine.py:76-148) takes [C,D,H,W] feature tensors + 4x4 voxel->world affines + a soft OCT mask and its only loss hook is loss_of (line 93, called at 134); new similarity = extra channels (vascular_refine pattern, vascular.py:89-97; zero edits to refine.py) or a Refiner subclass overriding loss_of (LCC/NGF). Restarts (register.py:171-178, 205-212) are diagnostic only - nothing is ever accepted/rejected on them, and the vascular result is accepted unconditionally (201); the fine stage needs its own acceptance gate. Ownership partition: A = octreg/specimen.py (new) + scripts/prep_subject.py; B = octreg/destripe.py (new) + common.py lines 181-211 only + scripts/test_destripe.py (new); C = octreg/fine.py (new) + scripts/register.py (+ viz_result.py/summarize.py). refine.py, search.py, features.py, vascular.py, evaluate.py frozen. Fragilities: unimodal-histogram fallback threshold (root cause of the 0.779 mask), prototype texture mask gives frac 0.18 on the brainstem (rim only, NOT usable as-is), largest-CC drops the separate tissue piece, no acceptance gate on refinement stages, fp16 cap/scale unbounded per slice, NIfTI OCT header affine ignored, viz_result hard-requires octv_vessels.npy, and rule (2) forces v1.1 prep into a NEW --work dir.

## 0. Data contract (what every implementer must preserve)

Conventions (common.py:1-12): arrays are (D,H,W) = NIfTI (i,j,k) for MRI and (Z=depth,Y,X) for OCT; every cache has a 4x4 float64 affine mapping voxel index -> world mm (voxel-centre convention: pooled_affine common.py:269-273 / avg_pool_iso 153-159 shift the origin by (k-1)/2). All transforms are world->world 4x4. sample_at_world (105-126) = trilinear grid_sample with zeros padding, align_corners=True; it is the single primitive used by search, refine, evaluate and all viz.

work/<SUBJ>/ (written by scripts/prep_subject.py):
- mri.npy float32 (I,J,K) native NIfTI order (line 71); mri_affine.npy = nibabel img.affine (voxel->RAS mm). xiangrui: (343,489,495) @ 0.08 mm.
- mri_tissue.npy bool same shape = mri > thr, thr from histogram_tissue_threshold(mri[::4,::4,::4]>0) (72-77); NO morphology, NO connected-component filter.
- labels4.npy uint8 {0,1 WM,2 infra,3 supra}, ba_labels.npy uint8, mri_vessels.npy bool: optional, MRI grid (83-98).
- oct_native_affine.npy = layout_affine(raw.shape, sp/1000, --oct-layout) (120): axis signs from the layout letters ('SPR'), origin 0, the OCT NIfTI header affine is IGNORED (spacing only, taken from header zooms as (z,y,x) at 109).
- oct150.npy float32 (Z,Y,X) shape150 (131) = floor(p150.shape * (sp*k150)/target); oct150_affine.npy: linear = sign*0.15 (132), translation = pooled_affine(A_nat,k150) (130). Values = slab-normalised, fp16-gained scattering (tissue median ~16384, cap 60000). xiangrui: (194,267,212), k150 = round(150/20)=8 (banker's rounding of 7.5) -> pooled at 160 um then trilinearly resampled to 150 um.
- oct150_mask.npy bool shape150 = oct_tissue_mask(o150, thresh=None, closing_iter=2) (134): histogram threshold on [::2] subsample -> >thr -> closing(2) -> fill_holes -> LARGEST CC ONLY (common.py:240-254).
- octv.npy float16 (Z,Y,X) = pool_mean_np(octn, kv) with kv = ceil(24/sp) (138-139) -> 40 um for 20 um data: (728,1006,797); octv_affine.npy = pooled_affine(A_nat,kv).
- octv_mask.npy bool = mask150 resampled nearest onto the octv grid via inv(A150)@A_v (142-144) - relies on both affines sharing axes (true: both derive from A_nat).
- octv_vessels.npy bool = (Frangi dark-tube max over sigmas 24/36/53/72/106 um, one gamma per scale) > 99th percentile inside octv_mask, & octv_mask (147-164).
- oct_ves_dist48_own.npy float32 (um) EDT of ~octv_vessels max-pooled by k=round(48/sp_v) (=1 here, so the '48 um' grid is really 40 um), + _affine.npy (168-174). oct_ves_dist48_vesseg.npy optional (179-187).
- prep.json (35 loads existing; 189 writes): mri{file,shape,voxel_mm,tissue_thresh,tissue_fraction,n_peaks,peak_pos,valley_ratio,intensity_p50_p99}, oct{file,shape_native,spacing_um_zyx,layout,raw_tissue_thresh,slab_window,shape150,tissue_frac150,vessel_level_spacing_um,shape_v,own_vessel_voxels,own_vessel_frac48,frangi_sigmas_vox,frangi_gamma,per_slice_median_head[,vesseg]}, labels_* optional.

## 1. OCT specimen mask option (owner A)

Where the masks are made: prep_subject.py:134 `mask150, thr150 = oct_tissue_mask(o150, thresh=None, closing_iter=2)` -> common.py:240-254 -> histogram_tissue_threshold(vol[::2,::2,::2]) common.py:214-237. For the brainstem the OCT histogram is unimodal (peak ~17k): len(pk)>=2 fails at 229, so thr = min(p1, 0.5*multiotsu[0]) (228) ~ noise floor -> mask = everything except the black tiles -> frac 0.779 (prep.json oct.tissue_frac150). octv_mask is a nearest resample of mask150 (142-144); octv_vessels are thresholded INSIDE octv_mask (162: percentile taken over maskv voxels; 163: vmask &= maskv); the EDT (168-174) follows from vmask. So the ONLY place to change is line 134 (+ optionally the corner-tile handling); everything else inherits.

Downstream assumptions about oct150_mask (register.py): 45 load; 96 MO = float mask [1,D,H,W] -> pyramid(MO) 106 -> FFTSearcher oct_mask (soft, 0.6 mm) 142 and Refiner oct_mask (voxels with pooled mask > 0.05 become the sample points, refine.py:85-88) 127/129; 97 otsu_two_class(oct150, MO.bool()) - the Otsu threshold of the OCT two-class split is computed over the masked voxels, so with agarose inside the mask the split is (specimen vs agarose) rather than (bright vs dark tissue); 110-113 overlap gate V_o = mask.sum()*VOX_O^3, MIN_OV = min(--min-overlap, max(0.15, 0.8*V_m/V_o)) (today 0.8*13.3/28.9 = 0.368; with a correct 13 cm3 mask -> 0.82); 200 density_on_grid target_mask; 220 oct_class = where(oct_mask, ...); 228 gm_wm_overlap; 254 qc_figure percentiles. evaluate.py:47-69 and every fig/viz script index oct150[om] for display windows. No consumer erodes the mask; no consumer tolerates a mask with zero voxels (kthvalue/percentile on empty -> crash at prep 162 and vascular.py:67,80).

Auto fallback decision point: prep_subject.py right after line 134, inside the OCT branch. MRI tissue volume IS available there: info = prep.json loaded at 35 (also when --skip-mri, provided the MRI was prepped earlier into the same --work), info["mri"]["tissue_fraction"] * prod(shape) * prod(voxel_mm) mm3 (written at 79-80). OCT intensity-mask volume = mask150.sum() * target_mm^3. Rule: mode = --oct-mask; if 'auto': texture if (V_mri available and V_int > 1.5*V_mri) else intensity; if V_mri unavailable -> intensity + loud warning (or accept an explicit --mri-tissue-cm3 override). Add a sanity band: accept the texture mask only if 0.5*V_mri <= V_tex <= 1.5*V_mri, else fall back to intensity and record why.
Implementation contract for A: new module octreg/specimen.py with `oct_specimen_mask(o150: np.ndarray f32 ZYX, vox_mm: float, **params) -> (mask bool, info dict)`; prep_subject.py edits: (i) flag `--oct-mask {intensity,texture,auto}` next to line 31; (ii) replace line 134 by: mask_int,thr150 = oct_tissue_mask(...); mask_tex,tinfo = oct_specimen_mask(...) when mode != intensity; choose; (iii) line 135 save oct150_mask.npy = CHOSEN mask (keeps the consumer contract) plus oct150_mask_intensity.npy and oct150_mask_texture.npy for diagnostics; (iv) info["oct"] (175-178) gains mask_mode, tissue_frac150_intensity, tissue_frac150_texture, V_oct_cm3_{int,tex}, V_mri_cm3, mask_reason. Lines 142-164 (octv_mask, vessels, EDT) need NO change - they consume mask150. Do NOT touch common.histogram_tissue_threshold/oct_tissue_mask (DANDI subjects depend on them). Note for the mask algorithm (from results/final/v1/texture_mask_test.png): the prototype scripts/test_texture_mask.py (local std win 7 @0.15 mm, gaussian 2, Otsu, closing 2, fill, largest CC) yields frac 0.18 on the brainstem - it keeps only the boundary rim because the interior is smooth at 0.15 mm and the rim is open at the black corner tiles/bottom edge - so it is a starting point, not a drop-in; the specimen boundary rim is however sharp and continuous in the texture score, so a rim -> closed-boundary -> fill construction (or texture at the 0.04 mm octv level pooled to 0.15) is the direction. Decide explicitly whether to keep components other than the largest (the separate small tissue piece is real specimen and is present in the MRI, which has no CC filter).
register.py side (owner C, optional): log prep["oct"].get("mask_mode") into result.json and warn at 113 if V_o > 1.5*V_m ("OCT mask over-inclusive - re-prep with --oct-mask texture"). No --oct-mask flag in register.py (switching the mask at run time would desynchronise octv_mask/octv_vessels/EDT).

## 2. Destripe step in prep (owner B)

Exact slot: prep_subject.py between line 126 (`octn, slab = oct_slab_normalize(raw, tissue_thresh=thr_raw, window=window, out_dtype=np.float16); del raw`) and line 129-130 (`k150 = ...; p150 = pool_mean_np(octn, k150)`). Both oct150 (130-133) and octv (139) are pooled from octn, so a destripe here reaches every downstream product (mask, vessels, EDT, register features). Variables in scope: octn float16 (Z,Y,X) native = (1457,2013,1595) = 4.68 G voxels = 9.4 GB; slab dict {per_slice_median[z] (NaN where <2000 voxels above thr), reference, scale, window, tissue_thresh, gain}; window = max(10, round(1200/sp[0])) = 60 slices at 20 um (125; the '1.2 mm section period' is an assumption inherited from the 12 um DANDI data - verify against the per_slice_median sawtooth, whose resets give the true section boundaries and phase); sp (um z,y,x); A_nat; thr_raw.
fp16 gain trick to respect (common.py:201-209): gain = 16384/nanmedian(ref) puts the tissue median at ~16384; cap = 60000 (local variable at 204, NOT returned in the dict); values are clipped to [0,cap] before the fp16 cast (208-209); fp16 max is 65504. Any multiplicative destripe correction g>1 can push values past 65504 -> inf that poisons every downstream percentile (this was Bug 1 in HANDOFF) => after correction always np.clip(v, 0, 60000) then cast.
Memory budget (HANDOFF 10.3.3: cgroup 16 CPUs / 62 GiB, one heavy job at a time): at line 126 raw (nibabel np.asanyarray of the .nii.gz -> fully materialised float32, ~18.7 GB) is freed, octn 9.4 GB remains; a whole-volume float32 copy would cost 18.7 GB per temp (one fits, two do not). Rule: process in z-chunks (pool_mean_np's own convention, common.py:262: 64 slices -> 0.8 GB f32 per temp) and write back in place into octn; estimate the stripe model from cheap statistics (per-section mean/median images (Y,X) = 3.2 M floats each, or per-x-column profiles) rather than from full-res filtering. Stripe geometry as visible in the QC figures: streaks are vertical both in z-x planes and in en-face (y,x) slices, i.e. the pattern is a per-x-column gain that is constant along y and z within a section -> a 1-D profile per section (or per tile) suffices; section membership from floor(z/window) refined by the per_slice_median resets.
Contract for B: new module octreg/destripe.py exposing `destripe_inplace(octn, window: int, sp_um, cap: float = 60000.0, zchunk: int = 64, section_bounds=None, **params) -> dict(info)`; owner A inserts after line 126: `if a.destripe == "on": from octreg.destripe import destripe_inplace; info_ds = destripe_inplace(octn, window=window, sp_um=sp)` and adds `--destripe {off,on}` + info["oct"]["destripe"]. B may additionally edit common.py ONLY inside oct_slab_normalize (181-211): return "cap": cap in the dict (210), optionally clamp scale to [0.25,4] (200). B validates standalone with scripts/test_destripe.py on the cached octv.npy (float16 40 um, 1.17 GB, same normalisation/cap) and oct150.npy - no prep re-run needed for development. Alternative placement (cheaper, but changes the pipeline order): destripe octv (1.17 GB) and derive oct150 from destriped octv (pool by 4: 8 = 2x4 so block means coincide) - flag if chosen because prep.json/oct150 provenance changes.

## 3. Fine stage in register.py (owner C)

Where: after line 179 (`del ref03, ref015, lvl015, PO, PMask, FO, trials, tr, PM06, PT06`) the structural result is T_struct (162); the vascular block is 181-217 (T_final = T_struct.copy() at 187, replaced unconditionally at 201). Insert the fine stage after 217 (operating on T_final, i.e. after vascular if on) or make it an alternative branch to vascular. Available at that point: mri (mmap f32, 44), mri_tissue_all (44), A_mri, lo/hi region (51-57), FM_cpu [P(WM),P(GM)] float16 CPU maps on the region grid (68-69), MO (96), FO_bright_first (97) with polarity OCT_WM_BRIGHT (155), oct150/A_oct/oct_mask, c_o (47), BLOCK_R/BOX (115-117, recomputed 183-185), rng (171), transform_diff, RK (124). The MRI box pattern to reuse: 189-195 (vlo/vhi = world_bbox_to_voxel(A_mri, mri.shape, bc-BOX, bc+BOX) clipped to lo/hi, A_v, mri_v_reg, tis_v, FM2v = torch.stack of the FM_cpu crop). octv is NOT loaded in register.py today; for a 0.08/0.04 mm level add np.load(work/'octv.npy', mmap_mode='r') (f16), octv_affine.npy, octv_mask.npy. PMask/PO are deleted at 179 - either keep them or rebuild pyramid(MO, A_oct, VOX_O) (100-106).

Refiner construction (refine.py:76-91): Refiner(mri_feat [C,D,H,W] float, mri_affine 4x4, oct_feat [C,d,h,w], oct_affine 4x4, oct_mask [1,d,h,w] in [0,1], device, chan_w=None|[C]). It flattens the OCT tissue voxels (pooled mask > 0.05, line 85) into pts_o [N,3] world, weights w [N], features fo [C,N]; c_o = OCT block centre from the array corners (91). Levels are handled OUTSIDE the class: register.py pyramid() (100-106; factor = round(level/vox): OCT 0.6/0.3/0.15 -> 4/2/1; MRI 0.08 -> 8/4/2 = 0.64/0.32/0.16 mm, so the structural stage never uses native 0.08 mm MRI), MRIFeatures.pooled/region (78-94) and vascular_refine's avg_pool_iso loop (vascular.py:91-97, factors=(2,1) or (4,2,1)). refine() (110-144): params (r,t,ls,sh,mirror) from params_from_matrix about c_o; Adam + cosine; loss = loss_of(T) + reg*(|ls|^2+|sh|^2) (135); ls/sh clamped each step (139); returns the T with the lowest data loss seen (140-141); subsample= strides the flat point list (94) - the only memory knob for big point sets (use >=4 at a 0.08 mm level: octv pooled by 2 is 73 M voxels, 78% masked = 57 M points). ncc_channels(T) (100-108) gives per-channel diagnostics.
New similarity as EXTRA CHANNEL (no edit to refine.py): mirror vascular_refine (vascular.py:84-98): FM = cat([FM2, extra_m]), FO = cat([FO2, extra_o]), chan_w=[1,1,w,...]; suitable for anything expressible as dense per-voxel maps compared by global masked NCC: MIND-SSC (features.mind_ssc 26-47, 12 ch, [1,1,D,H,W] in; build_features('mind') 125-128 standardises inside tissue first; radius/dilation 2 vox = matched physical scale at 0.15 OCT vs 0.16 MRI), gradient-magnitude maps, or plain z-scored intensity (features.build_features('intensity') - note test_polish.py showed raw-intensity NCC at 0.32/0.16 mm scores 0.03 and drags the block 9.5 mm: an intensity channel needs an acceptance gate). MRI channels live on the MRI box grid (A_v), OCT channels on the oct150 grid (A_oct) or octv grid (A_vv); T maps OCT world -> MRI world.
New similarity as NEW LOSS: subclass Refiner in octreg/fine.py and override loss_of(self, T, subsample) (refine.py:93-97) - refine() calls only self.loss_of (134); reuse self.FM/self.A_M/self.pts_o/self.w/self.fo. LCC: precompute a block id per point (recompute idx = nonzero(mask>0.05) exactly as line 85, bid = (idx//B) flattened) and accumulate the six weighted sums per block with index_add_, NCC per block, weighted mean -> 1-LCC. NGF: sample 3 MRI gradient channels via sample_at_world at T.pts_o, rotate the precomputed OCT gradients by M^-T (M=T[:3,:3]) and use the squared normalised dot product; MIND avoids the vector-rotation issue, so recommended order: mind (channel route) -> lcc (loss route) -> ngf.
Restart/acceptance logic today: structural candidates are ranked purely by loss (refine_level 130-136, best = lvl015[0] 148, polarity by min loss 155); the 12 perturbed restarts (171-178) and 8 vascular restarts (205-212) only COUNT convergence (corner_mean_mm < 0.5 / < 0.3 vs the solution) - they never replace T even when a restart reaches a lower loss; the vascular T is accepted unconditionally (201). Fine-stage acceptance to implement in fine.py: run from T_start (=T_final) plus K perturbed restarts (pattern 205-210 with compose/params_from_matrix); accept T_fine only if (a) fine loss(T_fine) < fine loss(T_start), (b) structural NCC at 0.15 (a Refiner on FM2v/FO2v like ref015) drops by < 0.02, (c) transform_diff(T_fine, T_start).corner_mean_mm <= --fine-clamp-derived cap (e.g. 5 mm, the residual is 'a few mm'), (d) >= half of the restarts land within 0.3 mm of T_fine; otherwise keep T_start and log fine.accepted=false with all numbers.
Outputs/logging to add: log["fine"] = {mode, w, clamp, levels, ncc_channels_before/after, loss_before/after, vs_start: transform_diff, stretch_ijk_before/after, restarts{n, n_within_0.3mm, detail}, accepted, seconds}; np.save(out/'T_oct2mri_prefine.npy', T_start) and keep T_oct2mri.npy = accepted T_final (247) so viz_result.py's Ts{'structural','final'} (line 20) and fig_* scripts show the fine result without changes; change `evaluate_T(T_struct) if vasc else None` (231) and `g0 = ... if vasc` (240) to `if (vasc or fine_on)`; add 'fine' to the summary print (269-271) and a fine column in summarize.py:16-24 / line 30-32. --fine parsing next to --vascular at line 35; log["args"] (39) records it automatically.

- A (mask): NEW octreg/specimen.py; scripts/prep_subject.py (all edits: --oct-mask, --destripe flags, mask block 134-135, destripe call after 126, info["oct"] 175-178). Reads B's function by the agreed signature; does not edit common.py.
- B (destripe): NEW octreg/destripe.py; NEW scripts/test_destripe.py; octreg/common.py ONLY lines 181-211 (oct_slab_normalize: expose cap, optional scale clamp). No edits to prep_subject.py.
- C (fine): NEW octreg/fine.py; scripts/register.py; scripts/viz_result.py and scripts/summarize.py if columns are added. No edits to refine.py/vascular.py.
- Frozen for all: refine.py, search.py, features.py, vascular.py, evaluate.py, nonrigid.py, common.py outside 181-211.
- Operational: rule (2) forbids touching work/xiangrui_I58bs/, so v1.1 prep must target a NEW --work dir (e.g. work/probe_xr/<name>/xiangrui_I58bs_v11) with a full prep (MRI part is cheap; the OCT part re-reads the 13 GB .nii.gz and is the multi-10-minute step); register with --out under work/probe_xr/... as well. prep uses the GPU for resample_to_grid (133) and the Frangi pass (147-161).

caveats:
1. Root cause of the wrong mask: common.py:214-237 histogram_tissue_threshold has no valley for a unimodal OCT histogram (peak ~17k), so it falls to thr = min(p1, 0.5*multiotsu) (228) ~ noise floor; oct_tissue_mask then fills holes and keeps the largest CC (249-253), i.e. the whole agarose block minus the black corner tiles -> frac 0.779. Any texture/boundary mask must be validated on volume (13 cm3 target) - the existing prototype scripts/test_texture_mask.py gives frac 0.18 on the brainstem (rim only; results/final/v1/texture_mask_test.png), so it is NOT a drop-in.
2. Largest-connected-component filter (common.py:250-253) will delete the 'separate small tissue piece' of the specimen from any new mask, while mri_tissue.npy (prep 76) keeps every piece; decide deliberately (keep components > x% of the largest, or accept the asymmetry - it only reduces template mass, whereas including agarose corrupts the Otsu split at register.py:97 and the NCC).
3. Overlap gate register.py:110-113: MIN_OV = min(--min-overlap, max(0.15, 0.8*V_m/V_o)) relaxes the gate to 0.368 whenever the OCT mask is over-inclusive, allowing poses with 63% of the template off MRI tissue to win; V_o is the bool 0.15 mm mask while the searcher's overlap (search.py:91) uses the soft 0.6 mm pooled mask; once the mask is fixed the gate returns to 0.82 and the FFT search behaviour changes - re-verify the pose after re-prep, do not assume the structural pose is unchanged.
4. No mask erosion anywhere: Refiner samples every voxel with pooled mask > 0.05 (refine.py:85) including partial-volume boundary voxels; otsu_two_class (features.py:51-65) blurs (sigma 1 vox) across the specimen/agarose boundary; boundary contamination grows if the new mask hugs the specimen tightly - consider a 1-voxel erosion for the Otsu statistics only (owner C/A decision, not present today).
5. fp16 guard (common.py:200-209): scale[i] = ref/med_f is unbounded per slice (a slice with few/low tissue voxels but > 2000 above thr gets a huge scale, saturating the whole plane at cap 60000); cap is a local variable not returned; the slab normalisation's 'tissue' median uses thr_raw = 0.5*Otsu of the raw subsample, which for this pair is ~0 (log: 'raw tissue thr 0.0'), so the per-slice median is over agarose+tissue+noise; the specimen mask exists only after pooling, so a mask-aware normalisation would need a second prep pass.
6. Destripe memory: any whole-volume float32 temp is 18.7 GB; two of them plus octn exceed the 62 GiB cgroup; corrections must be applied chunk-wise in place and re-clipped to [0,60000] before the fp16 cast (fp16 max 65504) - otherwise inf reappears in octv/oct150 and every percentile/kthvalue downstream breaks (prep 162, vascular.py:67,80, features.py:139).
7. Restart logic is diagnostic only (register.py:171-178, 205-212): a restart that finds a lower loss at a different pose is counted as 'not converged' and discarded; the vascular result is accepted unconditionally (201) - which is exactly how the vascular stage was allowed to move this pair 2.65 mm to a worse pose; test_polish.py showed a raw-intensity fine NCC (0.03) drags the block 9.5 mm. The fine stage must carry its own acceptance gate.
8. Data-contract traps: the OCT NIfTI header affine is ignored (prep 109 takes only zooms; A_nat from --oct-layout with origin 0), so T_oct2mri is defined w.r.t. oct150_affine, not the file's own world frame; k150 = round(7.5) = 8 (banker's rounding) so oct150 is a 160->150 um resample; the '48 um' EDT grid is 40 um for 20 um data (k = round(48/40) = 1); MRI structural levels are 0.64/0.32/0.16 mm, never native 0.08.
9. viz_result.py:28 hard-requires octv_vessels.npy/octv_affine.npy; prep line 162 (np.percentile over maskv voxels) and 163 crash or degenerate if the new mask is empty on the octv grid; with a tight specimen mask the vessel count will change drastically (today 4.5 M seam-artefact voxels) - keep --vascular off for this pair regardless.
10. Rule (2): work/xiangrui_I58bs/ must not be modified, so v1.1 prep needs a NEW --work dir and a full re-read of the 13 GB .nii.gz (raw is materialised to ~18.7 GB float32 by np.asanyarray at prep 107); run one heavy job at a time (HANDOFF 10.3.3); prep needs the GPU at lines 133 and 147-161 - a CPU-only probe run of the full prep is slow (Frangi on 584 M voxels) and should skip the vessel block if only the mask/destripe are being tested.
11. Minor: BLOCK_R/BOX are computed twice (register.py:115-117 and 183-185); pool_mean_np drops trailing remainders (common.py:260) so pooled grids can lose up to k-1 voxels per axis; pyramid() at register.py:104 caches by factor, so levels with equal factors alias (irrelevant today).
